name: Two-signal corroboration gate before any disruptive action
description: Blueprint 46 of 96 (BP-DBG-04 sibling; card BP-DBG-03). FLAGSHIP. Stands between a diagnosis and a DISRUPTIVE action - a restart, a kill, a rollback, a re-fix - and authorises it only when a second, mechanically INDEPENDENT probe agrees. The distinctive mechanism is the hard requirement that the SOURCE probe be declared: independence is a property of a pair, so an undeclared source is zero signals rather than one. That is the exact hole measured in the shipped implementation, where an absent source normalises to empty strings which any non-empty verifier trivially differs from, so the same-probe-rerun check cannot fire and the gate returns violations:[] with exit 0. Here a missing source is a FAILURE, and on disagreement the action is not authorised.

claim.description: The load-bearing claim that would authorise the action - 'the agents are stuck', 'mon is not on PATH', 'the PR's checks never ran'

source_probe.description: MANDATORY. The measurement that PRODUCED the claim, as an invocation. An empty or absent source is the measured hole this blueprint exists to close - it is a violation, never a pass.

candidate_verifier_probes.description: Candidate second signals. Re-running the source is not one of them.

action_reversibility.description: Worst-case default: an undeclared reversibility is treated as HARD (adverse inference), which is what makes this gate apply

claim-recorder.description: Records the claim WITH its producing probe. Refuses the record if the source probe is absent - that refusal is the whole point.

verifier-selector.description: Chooses a probe that differs MECHANICALLY - different shell, different data field, different measurement - and states how it differs

verifier-runner.description: Runs the chosen verifier and records the raw reading. Does not reconcile the two readings.

owner.description: The only actor that may authorise a hard-to-reverse action when the two signals disagree

routes.reason: the same model that produced the claim tends to pick a verifier that shares the claim's assumption

source-probe-declared.expression: source_probe_declared == true AND source_probe_nonempty == true AND source_probe_is_an_invocation == true

verifier-is-independent.expression: verifier_fingerprint != source_fingerprint AND verifier_is_source_rerun == false AND independence_dimension_named == true

stages.title: S0 DECLARE the probe that produced the claim - refuse the record without it

work_unit.title: Record every verdict together with its producing probe, and refuse any verdict that declares none
work_unit.question_or_target: Write the claim, the exact invocation that produced it, and that invocation's fingerprint into a claim record. If the source probe is absent, empty, or is prose rather than an invocation, emit FAILED - do NOT normalise it to an empty string, because an empty source trivially differs from any verifier and silently satisfies the independence check.

assigned_model_vendor_role.basis: this is the step whose absence produced a certified-but-uncorroborated claim in the shipped build

work_unit.evidence_requirement: the literal source invocation plus its output, and a fingerprint over (tool, shell, data-field, measurement-kind) - a prose description of how the claim was reached is NOT a source probe
tests_required: a CONFIRMED claim with an EMPTY source_probe must FAIL - run this against the current shipped gate first, where it returns violations:[] and exit 0, to prove the test can fail
a source_probe that is prose rather than an invocation must FAIL
both-states control: a properly declared source must PASS the same check, or the check rejects everything and measures nothing
work_unit.reviewer_requirement: an independent reviewer who re-runs the declared invocation and confirms it produces the recorded reading
work_unit.completion_sentinel: SUCCESS:ADV-0113 emitted only when claim-record.json exists, parses, and carries a non-empty source invocation, its raw output and its fingerprint; otherwise FAILED:ADV-0113 <reason>
work_unit.retry_policy: no retry: a second attempt to supply a source probe after the fact is a reconstruction, not a record - escalate instead

stages.title: An undeclared source is ZERO signals, not one - this gate is the measured fix
S1 SELECT a probe that differs mechanically, and NAME the dimension it differs on
Re-running the source probe is not a second signal
S2 RUN the independent verifier and record its raw reading
S3 If they disagree the FIRST reading was probably an artifact - investigate, do not act
S1b On disagreement, put the SOURCE probe through a both-states control before believing either reading
Record BOTH readings and the reconciliation - the pair is the evidence, not the winner
The action is authorised by the PAIR, or it is not authorised
A disruptive action on a disagreement needs the owner - and NEVER proceeds by timeout
stages.prompt: The two probes disagree, or one of them is unvalidatable. The pending disruptive action is NOT authorised by this gate. Authorise it explicitly, order a third measurement, or abandon it.

impact.blast_radius: the gate itself writes only under command-center/corroboration/**; its PURPOSE is to bound the blast radius of the disruptive action it gates, which it never performs

worked_example.scenario: Claim: 'mon is not on PATH'. Pending action: reinstall the tool and rewrite every caller.
worked_example.source_probe: `which mon` run in Git Bash -> not found
worked_example.verifier_selected: `Get-Command mon` in PowerShell 7. Independence dimension: DIFFERENT SHELL, and a different resolution rule - PowerShell resolves .cmd shims, MSYS which does not
worked_example.verifier_reading: resolves mon.cmd -> the claim is REFUTED and the reinstall is not authorised. The disruptive action would have been wasted work on a measurement artifact
worked_example.the_measured_hole: the shipped claim_gate.py validates id, text and verdict but NOT source_probe (_validate at :132-156); an absent source normalises to four empty strings at :173-185, which any non-empty verifier differs from, so same-probe-rerun cannot fire. A CONFIRMED claim with no source probe returns violations:[], ok:true, exit 0
worked_example.the_fix_here: source-probe-declared is BLOCKING with on_fail=fail, and the corresponding test is written to run against the CURRENT build first - where it must PASS the bad input - so the test is proven able to fail before it is trusted
worked_example.timeout_asymmetry: on_timeout is `fail`, not `escalate` or `proceed`: a destructive action must never become authorised because nobody answered

x_extensions.distinctive_mechanism: the SOURCE probe is a required, non-empty, invocation-shaped field, and independence is asserted as a named dimension between a declared pair rather than inferred from a string difference
contraindications: NOT for cheap reversible actions - just do it; the gate costs more than the mistake
NOT when the two available probes cannot be made independent - then the verdict is UNRESOLVED and the action stays unauthorised
NOT a document-level claim audit - this gates ONE claim at the moment it would authorise a destructive act
x_extensions.not_a_duplicate_because: the fresh-context blueprint re-derives a value in a CLEAN context; this corroborates one claim with a second probe in the SAME context, and its defining field is the declared source probe.
